title: fix(screenrecording): escalate webcam cleanup to SIGKILL and clear on stop-recording

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A stop during webcam startup kills the new overlay, then the first invocation starts recording anyway
leads.consequence: The webcam is spawned before gpu-screen-recorder and the start waits for map/resize plus 0.6 s; a second --stop-recording during that interval sees no recorder and newly calls cleanup_webcam. It kills the just-started overlay and exits 1, but does not cancel the first invocation. The first invocation resumes and starts a recording with no webcam overlay. ALT+PRINT also opens the capture menu because stop returned 1. Coordinate pending starts with stop or make stop cancel the pending recording rather than sweeping its overlay.
leads.triage: corroborated: Opus Q2 noted the narrow window; judged a minor behaviour change, not published

leads.summary: The early $* stop check misclassifies one quoted start argument as --stop-recording
leads.consequence: If mkdir fails and one argument contains a space followed by --stop-recording (for example '--webcam-device=absent --stop-recording'), $* matches the stop substring although the later per-argument parser does not set STOP_RECORDING. Instead of notifying and returning 1, it launches gpu-screen-recorder into a nonexistent output path and returns success in the tested stubbed failure case. Parse argv before guarding mkdir, or inspect each exact argv element.
leads.triage: factual, true by bash semantics but contrived; covered implicitly by suggestion to use $STOP_RECORDING after parsing; not published separately

leads.summary: The new redundant-stop cleanup does not refresh a stale recording indicator
leads.consequence: When gpu-screen-recorder was force-killed after stop_screenrecording refreshed the indicator, the bar may remain active. Every subsequent bar click runs --stop-recording. The new branch removes the overlay but immediately exits 1 without omarchy.indicators refresh, so the bar remains active and the button never returns to its start/menu action until an external refresh. Refresh after the recorder is gone and also in the inactive stop branch; related open #12471 changes exactly those points.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator: idle branch does not refresh indicators (only line 254 in stop path), but this is pre-existing and addressed by #12471; not a defect of this PR; dropped

leads.summary: Open PR #12021 implements the same issue with conflicting cleanup and stop hunks
leads.consequence: The two heads are diverged, not stacked. Both change cleanup_webcam and the inactive --stop-recording branch, producing two unresolved merge blocks whether based on the other PR's current base or the original common ancestor. #12021 uses ^mpv and waits up to 1 s, while this PR uses (^|/)mpv and a single 0.2 s grace; choosing #12021's regex also fails this PR's source-grep assertions. Choose one implementation and align/remove the other PR's duplicate change and tests before merging both. GitHub reports #12021 itself MERGEABLE against quattro, not mergeability with this head.
leads.triage: corroborated Opus F4; published in Other open PRs block

leads.summary: The new test append conflicts with the current quattro test changes
leads.consequence: The production script merges cleanly with the pinned current quattro tip, but the test file has a conflict at the same end-of-file append because quattro added runtime-state regression tests. Blindly taking either side drops the other tests. Rebase and keep both blocks: manually combined test and merged script passed in review.py (both statuses zero with process stubs). GitHub reports this PR CONFLICTING with quattro at intake.
leads.triage: corroborated Opus F4; published in Details (merge state)

leads.summary: The new stop test cannot detect a cleanup implementation that never actually signals an overlay
leads.consequence: Both SIGTERM and SIGKILL assertions grep the source text. The only new runtime assertion touches REGION_FILE and checks rm, without starting a matching overlay or checking a process died. In the isolated run pgrep always said no match and pkill always exited 1; the head test still passed all three new assertions. A plausible broken implementation with a matching but ineffective pkill therefore remains green. Add a TERM-ignoring synthetic overlay plus unrelated-process negative control in a PID-isolated test; do not run real pkill -f on the host.

leads.summary: The test always pre-creates Videos, leaving the new mkdir-on-start path untested
leads.consequence: A mutant that leaves the old 'missing directory' behavior or silently fails to create the directory still passes the new tests: the fixture creates OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DIR up front and never invokes a missing-directory start. Add a start case against a nonexistent writable output path and an uncreatable parent, checking directory creation, notification and exit status with safe stubs.
leads.triage: minor test gap for OUTPUT_DIR; subsumed by suggestion to drop the hunk; not published

leads.summary: The user manual states the reverse of the new directory creation behavior
leads.consequence: The published manual tells users that screen recording refuses to start if the output directory does not yet exist. The PR now mkdir -p's it and only refuses when creation fails. Replace the old pre-creation instruction with the new behavior and failure condition; otherwise users may unnecessarily create their own folders or misdiagnose a failure.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (manual/12-screenshots-recording.md:41 at head) and by Opus self-check; published as Impact of finding 2

leads.summary: The FAQ still tells users to create a recording directory themselves
leads.consequence: The FAQ says 'Just remember to create the directory you want to save to', but the PR creates an absent OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DIR on demand. Update this FAQ line to describe lazy creation and preserve the restart requirement for changes in the exported session environment.
leads.triage: verified (manual/46-faq.md:65); merged into DOC-MANUAL, not listed separately

leads.summary: The shipped session override example contains a stale create-it-yourself instruction
leads.consequence: The stock UWSM example for OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DIR still says '(remember to make the directory!)'. The recorder now creates a missing directory on start, so remove or qualify that instruction; copying/restoring this stock file via first-run or reset perpetuates the old behavior claim.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new `--stop-recording` test can stop a real recording; its assertions miss a broken escalation.

### New test signals real processes

The test runs the real script without stubbing `pgrep`/`pkill`, so it sends SIGINT to a running `gpu-screen-recorder` and still passes. **Impact:** a suite run during a recording stops it, and the assertions still pass with the `pkill -9` line removed.

**Suggested change:** stub `pgrep`/`pkill` and assert exit status and logged signals (block below).

<details><summary>Reproducer: the test stops a running recorder (at 800be974)</summary>

Save as `repro-test-signals-recorder.sh` and run from the repository root. It starts a stand-in recorder, so run it in a private PID namespace:

```
unshare --user --map-root-user --pid --fork --mount-proc bash repro-test-signals-recorder.sh
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Shows that test/shell.d/screenrecording-test.sh at the PR head signals a running
# screen recorder. Run it from the repository root inside a private PID namespace so
# nothing real can be reached, for example:
#   unshare --user --map-root-user --pid --fork --mount-proc bash repro-test-signals-recorder.sh
set -u
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# A stand-in for an in-progress recording: its command line starts with
# gpu-screen-recorder, and it notes SIGINT (the signal stop_screenrecording sends).
perl -e '$SIG{INT} = sub { open my $f, ">", $ARGV[0]; print $f "recorder got SIGINT\n"; exit 0 };
         $0 = "gpu-screen-recorder -w DP-1 -o /tmp/in-progress.mp4"; sleep 1 while 1' "$tmp/recorder" &
recorder=$!
sleep 0.5

bash test/shell.d/screenrecording-test.sh >"$tmp/test.log" 2>&1
echo "screenrecording-test.sh exit status: $?"
sleep 0.3
cat "$tmp/recorder" 2>/dev/null || echo "recorder was not signalled"
kill "$recorder" 2>/dev/null
wait 2>/dev/null
```

Actual output at the PR head (800be974):

```
screenrecording-test.sh exit status: 0
recorder got SIGINT
```

Actual output at the merge-base (86a2e583), same test file path, as a control:

```
screenrecording-test.sh exit status: 0
recorder was not signalled
```
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: tests pass without the SIGKILL, and a suggested replacement test</summary>

Save as `repro-mutant.sh` and run from the repository root at the PR head. The PR test signals real processes, so run it in a private PID namespace:

```
unshare --user --map-root-user --pid --fork --mount-proc bash repro-mutant.sh
```

```bash

# Run from the repository root at the PR head. The PR's test signals real processes, so
# run this inside a private PID namespace:

set -u
tmp=$(mktemp -d)

cp -r bin test default "$tmp/"

# Break the escalation: comment out the SIGKILL.
sed -i '/WebcamOverlay/ s/^    pkill -9/    : # pkill -9/' "$tmp/bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording"
diff -u bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording "$tmp/bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording" |
  sed "s|$tmp|\$tmp|g"

bash "$tmp/test/shell.d/screenrecording-test.sh" 2>&1 | tail -n 3

Actual output at the PR head (800be974):

```

+++ $tmp/bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording	2026-09-29 21:16:43.741324462 +0200
@@ -115,7 +115,7 @@

-    pkill -9 -f '(^|/)mpv.*WebcamOverlay' 2>/dev/null || true

Two further mutants also pass all 21 PR tests: inverting the check (`if ! pgrep -f ...`) and changing the idle `--stop-recording` branch to `exit 0` (which would stop the `ALT + PRINT` binding from opening the menu).

**Suggested replacement test**

Replace the three new assertions at the end of `test/shell.d/screenrecording-test.sh` with this block. It stubs `pgrep`/`pkill` (as other tests in the repository do), so it never signals real processes, and it checks the escalation, the region file and the exit status:

```bash
# cleanup_webcam and the idle --stop-recording branch. pgrep and pkill are stubbed
# so the test never signals the developer's own recorder or overlay; the stubs log
# every call and report a webcam overlay that survives SIGTERM when asked to.
cat >"$stub_bin/pgrep" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'pgrep %s\n' "$*" >>"$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG"
[[ $* == *WebcamOverlay* && ${OMARCHY_TEST_OVERLAY_STUCK:-false} == "true" ]]
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/pkill" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'pkill %s\n' "$*" >>"$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG"
SH
chmod +x "$stub_bin/pgrep" "$stub_bin/pkill"
export OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG="$tmp_dir/signal-log"

region_file="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-screenrecord-region"
: >"$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG"
touch "$region_file"
status=0
OMARCHY_TEST_OVERLAY_STUCK=true "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording" --stop-recording >/dev/null 2>&1 || status=$?
[[ $status == 1 ]] ||
  fail "--stop-recording without a recorder still exits 1 for the Alt+Print menu fallback" "status: $status"
pass "--stop-recording without a recorder still exits 1 for the Alt+Print menu fallback"
[[ ! -e $region_file ]] || fail "--stop-recording without a recorder clears the webcam region file"
pass "--stop-recording without a recorder clears the webcam region file"
grep -qxF 'pkill -f (^|/)mpv.*WebcamOverlay' "$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG" ||
  fail "--stop-recording without a recorder asks the webcam overlay to quit" "$(<"$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG")"
pass "--stop-recording without a recorder asks the webcam overlay to quit"
grep -qxF 'pkill -9 -f (^|/)mpv.*WebcamOverlay' "$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG" ||
  fail "a webcam overlay that ignores SIGTERM is killed" "$(<"$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG")"
pass "a webcam overlay that ignores SIGTERM is killed"

: >"$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG"
"$ROOT/bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording" --stop-recording >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if grep -q '^pkill -9' "$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG"; then
  fail "a webcam overlay that exits on SIGTERM is not SIGKILLed" "$(<"$OMARCHY_TEST_SIGNAL_LOG")"
fi
pass "a webcam overlay that exits on SIGTERM is not SIGKILLed"
```

Actual results (same block, in the review sandbox):

- PR head: all 23 tests pass; the new lines are:

ok - --stop-recording without a recorder clears the webcam region file

ok - a webcam overlay that exits on SIGTERM is not SIGKILLed
```

- PR head with the SIGKILL line commented out (the mutant above), stderr:

pkill -f (^|/)mpv.*WebcamOverlay

```

- PR head with the idle branch changed to `exit 0`, stderr:

```

not ok - --stop-recording without a recorder still exits 1 for the Alt+Print menu fallback
```

- Merge-base script, stderr:

</details>

### Missing recording directory is created silently

The `OUTPUT_DIR` hunk runs `mkdir -p` and notifies only if it fails, so a mistyped `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DIR` is created. **Impact:** this contradicts `manual/12-screenshots-recording.md`, and #11850 does not need it.

**Suggested change:** drop this hunk, or move the check below argument parsing and skip it when `$STOP_RECORDING` is true.

<details><summary>Reproducer: directory created without notification (at 800be974)</summary>

Save as `repro-output-dir.sh` and run from the repository root. The notification helper, region picker, `pgrep` and `pkill` are stubbed and the picker cancels, so nothing is recorded or signalled.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from the repository root. Safe on a desktop: the notification helper, the region
# picker, pgrep and pkill are stubbed, and the picker "cancels" so nothing is recorded.
set -u
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmp/bin"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "notification: $*"\n' >"$tmp/bin/omarchy-notification-send"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' >"$tmp/bin/omarchy-capture-region"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' >"$tmp/bin/pgrep"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' >"$tmp/bin/pkill"
chmod +x "$tmp/bin"/*

# A recording directory that does not exist, e.g. a typo or an unmounted drive.
PATH="$tmp/bin:$PWD/bin:$PATH" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$tmp" OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DIR="$tmp/typo/Videos" \
  bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording 2>&1 | sed "s|$tmp|\$tmp|g"
echo "exit status: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
[[ -d $tmp/typo/Videos ]] && echo "\$tmp/typo/Videos now exists" || echo "\$tmp/typo/Videos was not created"
```

Actual output at the PR head (800be974):

```
exit status: 0
$tmp/typo/Videos now exists
```

Actual output at the merge-base (86a2e583):

```
notification: -u critical -t 3000 Screen recording directory does not exist: $tmp/typo/Videos
exit status: 1
$tmp/typo/Videos was not created
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox, real mpv 0.41.0 blocked in a read that its SIGTERM handling cannot cancel, plus stand-in processes):
- `cleanup_webcam` kills an overlay `mpv` that ignores SIGTERM (about 0.21 s); the merge-base cleanup left it alive.
- The new pattern leaves a user's `mpv ~/Videos/...` and the script's own `jq` polling alone, and no longer kills a shell whose own command line contains the cleanup command.
- An idle `--stop-recording` removes a stranded overlay and still exits 1, so the `ALT + PRINT` menu fallback keeps working.

**Merge state:** the script merges cleanly into current `quattro`. `test/shell.d/screenrecording-test.sh` conflicts, because both sides append tests at the end. Keeping both blocks (`quattro`'s first) resolves it, but `quattro`'s `pgrep` stub then runs before this PR's stop test, so the escalation is never reached there.

**Optional:** the fixed `sleep 0.2` SIGKILLs a healthy overlay that needs longer than 0.2 s to exit (a 300 ms stand-in was killed); polling `pgrep` for up to about 1 s would let it exit cleanly.
</details>

<details><summary>Other open PRs for this issue</summary>

- #12021: same two script changes (SIGKILL escalation, idle-stop cleanup) with an anchored `^mpv` pattern and polling for up to 1 s before SIGKILL; no test or `OUTPUT_DIR` changes. It conflicts with this PR in `bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording`.
</details>
